responses.spec:
# Pilot Detection Checklist

Status: Validated
Specification Version: v1
Frozen: true
Type: General
Readiness Contract: evidence-v1

## Decision Record

| ID | Decision | Basis / evidence | Remaining uncertainty, consequence, and check | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Use the manual Friday-review process for this pilot; decline automation | Decided: user statement, "use the manual process for this pilot" / "declined automation for the pilot" | None — explicit choice for pilot scope | resolved |
| D2 | Accept up to seven days of detection delay inherent to a weekly manual review | Decided: "The owner explicitly accepts up to seven days of detection delay" | Latency up to 7 days is possible before a missed alert surfaces; checked by the two-Friday inspection in D4 | accepted-uncertainty |
| D3 | Owner is personally responsible for the review | Decided: owner "assigned herself" to this role | None | resolved |
| D4 | Owner inspects missed alerts after two Fridays as the pilot's check on D2 | Decided: owner assignment statement | None — this is the concrete check for the accepted delay | resolved |
| D5 | Checklist is the only deliverable; no systems change | Decided: "The checklist is the only deliverable; no systems change" | None | resolved |

## Decision History

_No superseded decisions._

## Critique Reconciliation

| Finding ID | Source / specification version | Disposition | Reason / incorporated change |
|---|---|---|---|
_None received._

## Problem Statement

The reporting team needs a documented pilot checklist for detection review that uses the existing manual Friday review, records the accepted detection-delay tradeoff, assigns ownership, and sets a review checkpoint — without introducing any automation or systems change.

## Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Observable acceptance criterion | Decision / evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Checklist states the review occurs via the existing manual Friday review | Checklist contains an item naming the weekly Friday review as the detection mechanism | D1 |
| R2 | Checklist states the accepted detection delay | Checklist contains an item stating up to seven days of detection delay is accepted for this pilot | D2 |
| R3 | Checklist names the owner's responsibility | Checklist contains an item naming the owner as responsible for conducting the review | D3 |
| R4 | Checklist includes the two-Friday inspection checkpoint | Checklist contains an item specifying that the owner inspects missed alerts after two Fridays | D4 |

## Constraints

- No automation is introduced; the pilot uses the existing manual process only (D1, D5).
- The checklist document is the sole deliverable of this task; no system, tool, or process changes accompany it (D5).

## Success Criteria

Done means the checklist contains all four items in R1–R4 and introduces no automation or systems change (D5).

## Validation Contract

### Acceptance Tests

- Read-through of the completed checklist confirms all four items (R1–R4) are present and each names the specific fact required (weekly Friday review, 7-day accepted delay, owner's name/role, two-Friday inspection checkpoint).

### Regression Checks

Not applicable — no systems or code change is in scope (D5).

### Failure Signals

Checklist is missing one of the four required items, or includes any automation/system-change element, which would contradict D5.

### Verification Methods

Manual inspection of the checklist text against R1–R4 by the owner or reviewer.

### Feedback Loop Design

The two-Friday inspection (D4) is the pilot's live feedback loop for the accepted detection delay (D2); no additional cadence is implied beyond what was decided.

### Known Blind Spots

Detection delay up to 7 days is accepted as a known limitation (D2), checked only at the two-Friday mark, not continuously.

## Inputs

Existing manual Friday review process; owner's decisions as recorded in D1–D5.

## Outputs

A written pilot checklist document containing the four required items.

## Out of Scope

Any automation, tooling, or system changes to the detection or review process (D1, D5).

## Authority Boundaries

### Executor May Decide

Checklist formatting, wording, and layout, provided all four required items (R1–R4) are present and accurate.

### Executor Must Escalate

Any proposal to introduce automation or systems change during the pilot.

### Executor Must Not Change

The four decided facts (D1–D4) or the "checklist only, no systems change" constraint (D5).

## Current Interpretation

Produce a single checklist document for the pilot that documents the manual Friday review, the accepted 7-day detection delay, the owner's responsibility, and the two-Friday missed-alert inspection — nothing else changes.

## Misclassification Risks

### Potential False Positives

A checklist that mentions the four topics only in passing, without them being identifiable as discrete items, could be miscounted as satisfying R1–R4.

### Potential False Negatives

None identified — the four items are simple factual statements that either appear or do not.

## Ambiguities

### Blocking

_None._

### Non-Blocking

_None._

### Intentional

- Exact wording/format of each checklist item is left to the executor (delegated, not an open decision).

## Risks

Detection delay up to 7 days during the pilot window, explicitly accepted per D2 and checked via D4.

## Stakeholders

Reporting team owner (decision-maker and executor of the Friday review and the two-Friday inspection).
